--- title: "Chapter 9: Difference-in-Differences" jupyter: mixtape-causalpy --- ## Causal Inference: The Mixtape → CausalPy **Mixtape chapter**: [Difference-in-Differences](https://mixtape-1ed.netlify.app/09-difference_in_differences.html) **CausalPy method**: [`StaggeredDifferenceInDifferences`](https://causalpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/generated/causalpy.experiments.staggered_did.StaggeredDifferenceInDifferences.html) for the castle-doctrine panel. [`DifferenceInDifferences`](https://causalpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notebooks/difference-in-differences-pymc.html) estimates one group-by-post interaction. It is not the castle result. ## Overview Adoption dates in the castle-doctrine panel are not a single year. A two-group, two-period coefficient is the wrong estimand for that design, and it is not what this page reports. The fit below is the Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess imputation estimator [@borusyak2024]. The untreated outcome is a Bayesian linear model. It is not Cheng and Hoekstra's two-way fixed-effects coefficient [@cheng2013], and it is not `castle_1.py`. Snow, the minimum wage, block bootstrap, clustering, the Affordable Care Act, and maternity benefits have no script on this page. No dataset is added for them. ## Setup ::: {#2469baba .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") import numpy as np import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import causalpy as cp import sys sys.path.insert(0, "../src") from mixtape_causalpy import load_castle, load_abortion %matplotlib inline %config InlineBackend.figure_format = 'retina' ``` ::: ## Castle doctrine `castle.dta` is a state-year panel. `treatment_date` is the adoption year, and it is missing for states with no recorded adoption. The outcome used here is `l_homicide`, the log homicide rate. `DifferenceInDifferences` estimates a single group-by-post interaction. That is not this panel, and it is not used as the result. ### Adoption timing ::: {#18402776 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} castle = load_castle().copy() castle["treatment_time"] = castle["treatment_date"].astype(float) n_missing_dates = int(castle["treatment_time"].isna().sum()) castle.loc[castle["treatment_time"].isna(), "treatment_time"] = np.inf timing = castle.groupby("state", as_index=False)["treatment_date"].first() n_states = int(timing["state"].nunique()) n_years = int(castle["year"].nunique()) n_never = int(timing["treatment_date"].isna().sum()) panel_start = int(castle["year"].min()) earliest_adoption = int(timing["treatment_date"].min()) timing["adoption"] = timing["treatment_date"].apply( lambda v: "no adoption date" if pd.isna(v) else str(int(v)) ) year_order = sorted(y for y in timing["adoption"].unique() if y != "no adoption date") adoption_counts = ( timing.groupby("adoption").size().reindex(year_order + ["no adoption date"]) ) print( f"{n_states} states, {n_years} years, {n_never} with no adoption date" ) print(f"Panel starts in {panel_start}; earliest recorded adoption is {earliest_adoption}") print(f"Missing treatment_date rows before recode: {n_missing_dates}") print(adoption_counts.to_string()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 50 states, 11 years, 29 with no adoption date Panel starts in 2000; earliest recorded adoption is 2005 Missing treatment_date rows before recode: 319 adoption 2005 3 2006 11 2007 4 2008 2 2009 1 no adoption date 29 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-castle-adoption .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4)) ax.bar(adoption_counts.index.astype(str), adoption_counts.values, color="C0") ax.set_xlabel("Recorded adoption year") ax.set_ylabel("States") ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![States by recorded castle-doctrine adoption year, including states with no adoption date in the file.](09_difference_in_differences_files/figure-html/fig-castle-adoption-output-1.png){#fig-castle-adoption width=951 height=380} ::: ::: The file stores a missing `treatment_date` for 29 states. `StaggeredDifferenceInDifferences` rejects missing treatment times. It does not read a missing date as never-treated. Those dates are recoded to `np.inf`, the class default for never-treated, before the fit. The states stay in the panel and are the never-treated controls. None are dropped. There is no already-treated cohort in the first year. The panel starts in 2000 and the earliest recorded adoption is 2005. ### Imputation event-time contrasts The formula is state and year fixed effects. `C()` accepts the numeric year column, so year is not recoded to a string. The `1` in the formula is the intercept column of the design matrix. The Bayesian model multiplies that matrix by its coefficient vector and does not add a second intercept. `post` is an absorbing 0/1 column in the file. It is not passed as `treated_variable_name`. The absorbing-treatment check runs only when that argument is passed. `l_homicide` has no missing values, so there is nothing for a missing-outcome check to drop. The class's missing-value check on a treated column is about the treatment indicator, not the outcome. ::: {#b060120f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} result = cp.StaggeredDifferenceInDifferences( castle, formula="l_homicide ~ 1 + C(state) + C(year)", unit_variable_name="state", time_variable_name="year", treatment_time_variable_name="treatment_time", model=cp.pymc_models.LinearRegression( sample_kwargs={ "chains": 2, "tune": 100, "draws": 200, "progressbar": True, "random_seed": 42, } ), ).fit() result.summary() castle_att = result.result.att_event_time att0 = castle_att.loc[castle_att["event_time"] == 0].iloc[0] att_m1 = castle_att.loc[castle_att["event_time"] == -1].iloc[0] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` NUTS[nutpie]: [beta, y_hat_sigma] ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

`att` is the posterior mean of the unit-averaged imputation contrast at that event time: observed log homicide minus the untreated prediction. It is not normalized to a zero reference period. The constructor's `reference_event_time` defaults to −1 and is reserved for plots; it does not subtract that cell from the others. Event time −1 is \-0\.016, not zero. Event time 0, the adoption year, is \+0\.062 log points, from 21 state-years. Its 94% interval is \[\+0\.013\, \+0\.109\].

`att_lower` and `att_upper` are the 3rd and 97th percentiles of that contrast. The plot labels those bars as a 94% HDI. They are not residual standard errors, and a cell with one observation still has a bar. `nuts_sampler` is omitted, so the installed nutpie sampler is selected. No `cores` argument is passed.

That event-time 0 number is not Cheng and Hoekstra's two-way fixed-effects coefficient. This page does not estimate that coefficient, so the two are not compared.

::: {.callout-note}
## What this fit is not

This is not `castle_1.py`. That script regresses log homicide on an absorbing treatment indicator, state and year effects, and region-by-year effects, with standard errors clustered by state. This page does not estimate that coefficient.

`castle_2.py` is an event study with leads and lags, estimated by weighted least squares, with region-by-year effects and clustered standard errors. `castle_3.py` and `castle_4.py` plot those weighted least-squares estimates. CausalPy does not implement that weighted least-squares event study. The table above is the imputation substitute, not those figures.

`castle_5.py` is empty. The R script decomposes `l_homicide ~ post` with the Bacon decomposition. It is not run.

[PR #584](https://github.com/pymc-labs/CausalPy/pull/584) is an open proposal for a common-timing event study. It is not this staggered design, and it is not a castle-doctrine specification.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Bacon decomposition and triple differences

A Bacon decomposition would split a two-way fixed-effects coefficient into timing comparisons. CausalPy does not implement it, and none is computed. This file also has no already-treated cohort in 2000.

Triple differences (`abortion_ddd.py`, `abortion_ddd2.py`) are not in CausalPy. The write-up is [`proposals/proposal_triple_diff.md`](../proposals/proposal_triple_diff.md). That proposal is not a Bacon decomposition.
:::

## Abortion legalization

The book's abortion exercise is a two-way fixed-effects regression. Treatment is an early-repeal indicator interacted with year, on state-years from 1985 to 2000, with state and year effects and controls. A split of the sample at 1993 is not that design. It is not used here, and the regression is not fit.

::: {#ad5d438f .cell execution_count=6}

``` {.python .cell-code}
print(f"Rows: {len(abortion)}; years {int(abortion['year'].min())}–{int(abortion['year'].max())}")
print(abortion["repeal"].value_counts(dropna=False).to_string())
```

## Abortion scripts are not run

`abortion_dd.py` and `abortion_dd2.py` are the two-way fixed-effects regressions above. `DifferenceInDifferences` estimates one group-by-post interaction, which is not those regressions. Neither is run on this page.
:::

## Summary

One estimator is run: the imputation event-time contrasts for castle doctrine. The two-way fixed-effects castle coefficient, the weighted least-squares event study, the Bacon decomposition, the abortion two-way fixed effects, and triple differences are callouts. They are not counted as completed reproductions of those scripts.

::: {.callout-note}
